name: Direct Context Injection
intent: Answer from a small, static corpus placed directly in the prompt — no retrieval infrastructure.
description: The entire relevant corpus fits in the model's context window and changes rarely. No retriever, no index, no reranker.
preconditions: Corpus fits comfortably within the target model's context window
No per-user filtering of the corpus is required
escalation_trigger: the corpus grows too large to fit in context, needs per-user access control, or changes frequently
mermaid_template:
flowchart LR
  U[User query] --> P[Prompt incl. full corpus]
  P --> G[Generator model]
  G --> A[Answer]

name: Single-Pass RAG (hybrid retrieval + rerank)
intent: Retrieval-augmented generation over an indexed enterprise document store — the default enterprise baseline for grounded Q&A.
description: The model answers or drafts using retrieved passages instead of relying on parametric memory alone. Hybrid (lexical + vector) retrieval with a reranking pass.
preconditions: A retrievable, indexable corpus exists or can be built
escalation_trigger: questions typically require multiple retrieval steps, or are frequently ambiguous
mermaid_template:
flowchart LR
  U[User query] --> R[Retriever]
  R --> IDX[(Document Index)]
  R --> G[Generator model]
  G --> A[Answer with citations]

name: Agentic RAG
intent: Query planning, iterative retrieval, and self-checking over the corpus — for questions a single retrieval pass cannot answer.
description: The model plans a sequence of retrieval steps, checks intermediate evidence, and re-queries before answering.
preconditions: Single-pass retrieval has been evaluated and shown insufficient, or the requirement set predicts it will be
escalation_trigger: answering questions requires tracing relationships between entities, not just retrieving passages
mermaid_template:
flowchart LR
  U[User query] --> PL[Query planner]
  PL --> R1[Retrieval step 1]
  R1 --> CHK{Sufficient?}
  CHK -- no --> R2[Retrieval step 2]
  CHK -- yes --> G[Generator model]
  R2 --> CHK
  G --> A[Answer with citations]

name: GraphRAG
intent: Answer questions that require traversing entity relationships a document retriever cannot see.
description: Requires a maintained entity graph — a standing data-engineering obligation, not a retrieval tweak.
preconditions: An entity/relationship model exists or the organisation commits to maintaining one
mermaid_template:
flowchart LR
  U[User query] --> R[Retriever]
  R --> GDB[(Entity Graph)]
  R --> G[Generator model]
  G --> A[Answer]

name: Fine-Tuning for Knowledge Injection
intent: Bake proprietary knowledge into model weights instead of retrieving it at query time.
description: Contra-indicated whenever attribution or freshness matters — a fine-tuned model cannot cite a source span and cannot be kept current without retraining. Legitimate only for style/format/vocabulary adaptation, never as a substitute for retrieval.
preconditions: A labelled or representative training set of sufficient size exists
mermaid_template:
flowchart LR
  DS[(Training examples)] --> FT[Fine-tuning job]
  FT --> M[Adapted model]
  U[User query] --> M
  M --> A[Answer]

name: Real-time Copilot Sidecar
intent: Suggest actions or draft content alongside an existing application surface, without taking action itself.
description: A low-latency assistant embedded alongside an existing application, suggesting as the user works.
preconditions: A host application surface exists to embed alongside
escalation_trigger: the assistant needs to take action on a system of record, not just suggest
mermaid_template:
flowchart LR
  APP[Host application] -- context --> SC[Copilot sidecar]
  SC --> M[Low-latency model]
  M --> SC
  SC -- suggestion --> APP

name: Agentic Workflow with Human-in-the-loop
intent: Plan and execute a multi-step workflow across enterprise systems, pausing for human approval at defined checkpoints.
description: A single agent with planning and constrained tool calling, gated by human checkpoints rather than acting fully autonomously.
preconditions: The workflow's tools/systems have callable, bounded interfaces
escalation_trigger: the work splits into independent tasks that different teams own
mermaid_template:
flowchart LR
  U[Trigger] --> AG[Agent planner]
  AG --> T1[Tool / system call]
  AG --> CP{Checkpoint}
  CP -- approve --> T2[Next action]
  CP -- reject --> H[Human edits plan]
  T2 --> DONE[Workflow complete]

name: Autonomous Multi-Agent Orchestration
intent: Coordinate multiple specialised agents on a shared objective with minimal human checkpoints.
description: Each agent owns a distinct sub-task; an orchestrator reconciles results. Cross-organisational or independently-deployed agents are where this earns its place.
preconditions: Sub-tasks are genuinely independent and separately owned
mermaid_template:
flowchart LR
  ORC[Orchestrator agent] --> A1[Sub-agent: research]
  ORC --> A2[Sub-agent: execution]
  ORC --> A3[Sub-agent: verification]
  A1 & A2 & A3 --> ORC
  ORC --> OUT[Objective complete]

name: Batch Classification Pipeline
intent: Classify or score a high volume of records on a schedule or trigger, without a human in the loop per record.
description: A scheduled or event-triggered pipeline scoring records against a fixed label set.
preconditions: A fixed, well-defined label set exists
mermaid_template:
flowchart LR
  SRC[(Source records)] --> Q[Batch queue]
  Q --> CL[Classifier model]
  CL --> OUT[(Scored output store)]

name: Input/Output Guardrails
intent: Filter untrusted input and model output for injection attempts, policy violations, and PII/PHI leakage.
description: Cross-cutting assurance pattern. Required whenever untrusted input meets a model — essentially always in an enterprise context. Not a design choice to be scored; an obligation-derived requirement.
mermaid_template:
flowchart LR
  IN[Input] --> GI[Input guardrail]
  GI --> M[Model]
  M --> GO[Output guardrail]
  GO --> OUT[Output]

name: Grounded-Answer Evaluation Harness
intent: Continuously measure output quality so regressions are detectable.
description: Required for any pattern whose output quality is not deterministically verifiable — if you cannot measure whether it is getting worse, you cannot operate it.
mermaid_template:
flowchart LR
  M[Model output] --> E[Eval harness]
  GS[(Golden set)] --> E
  E --> R[Quality report]

name: Observability & Tracing
intent: Capture trace, cost, latency, token, tool-call and retrieval logging for every request.
description: Required for every production AI component, PHI-safe where applicable.
mermaid_template:
flowchart LR
  M[Model / pipeline] --> T[Trace + cost + latency logs]
  T --> D[Observability dashboard]

name: Authorisation Propagation
intent: Propagate the caller's identity to every downstream data or action call.
description: Required whenever retrieval or actions touch permissioned data — a structural property of the retrieval/action layer, not a feature to consider.
mermaid_template:
flowchart LR
  U[Caller identity] --> P[Identity propagation layer]
  P --> DS[(Downstream data / action)]

name: Human Oversight Gate
intent: Route output or actions through a human review step, from post-hoc sampling up to mandatory pre-action approval.
description: Level is set by the oversight ladder trigger: informational/reversible needs no gate; irreversible or regulated actions need pre-action approval.
mermaid_template:
flowchart LR
  OUT[Proposed output / action] --> HG{Human gate}
  HG -- approve --> EXEC[Executed]
  HG -- reject --> REV[Revise]
